scenes.headline: How AVM remembers a room without building it
scenes.sub: Meta and Oxford's Autoregressive View Model
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Homeward! This is AVM. It keeps a scene as a pile of views, and looks them up by where the camera stands.

scenes.title: Two ways to answer: render this camera

left.title: Gaussian splat
items: Every render agrees with every other
Knows nothing you did not photograph
left.say: A splat fits geometry once. Every render agrees, but it knows nothing you did not photograph.

right.title: AVM
items: Keep every posed view in a pool
Generate short clips from retrieved views
Invents what the photos never saw
right.say: AVM keeps the views themselves, and generates new ones from them. It can invent what the photos missed.

steps.term: Pool: every view, given or generated
steps.say: Every view, the photos you give it and the frames it makes, goes into one pool, tagged with its camera pose.
Before each chunk, it fetches the few old views whose cameras could see what the next camera will see.
Add the prefill sink and the last few frames, and the transformer generates the next short clip.
Those frames join the pool. The pool grows forever. What the model attends to stays small.

params.pool: Every view drops into the pool where it was taken
params.motion: The motion window: its own recent frames
params.cover: Retrieved by pose: the views taken here on the way out

steps.say: Here is that in a toy, from above. The camera slides along a room, out and back, and every view lands in the pool where it was taken.
On the way back, the motion window holds the last few frames. They are the model's own recent output, so any error in them carries forward.

steps.term: Retrieval: old views whose cones cover the target's
steps.say: So fetch by pose. The views taken at this spot on the way out see the same wall, and so does the original photo. Now the model can copy the room as it first saw it.

scenes.title: Revisit PSNR on loop paths
scenes.note: the paper's numbers, its own benchmark
scenes.say: The paper's ablation says it is the lookup doing the work. Revisit PSNR is twenty-eight with retrieval, and eleven without it, level with the best world model.

scenes.title: From a video model to a streaming one

steps.say: Underneath is Wan, a fourteen billion parameter image to video model.

steps.term: N-in-1-out: many context slots, one target clip
steps.say: It is fine-tuned to take many context slots, images, clips or other cameras, and produce one target clip.
Then it is made causal, block by block, so finished frames can be cached.
And it is distilled on its own long rollouts, with the same retrieved context it will see at inference.
The paper's comparisons: from a few posed photos, against a view synthesis model.
And on a revisit, where a world model without retrieval comes back to a different room.

items.say: It follows text prompts worse than the world models do.

items.text: The least motion of the four
items.say: It moves the camera well and the world less.
And there is no speed figure, no code and no weights yet.

scenes.text: The memory is an index: posed views, fetched by what the next camera will see. Attention stays bounded.
scenes.mark: fetched by what the next camera will see
scenes.say: The idea to keep is the index. File every view by pose, fetch by what the next camera will see, and the attention stays small however long you walk.

recap: A scene as a pool of posed views
scenes.say: A pool of posed views, fetched by coverage, and a room that is still there when you come back.
